artworks.title: Lydia Viscardi – Time Takes Time
artworks.description: October 31, 2026 – January 10, 2027 Lydia Viscardi – Time Takes Time presents a body of mixed-media work that considers the passage of time and the cycles of the seasons within the changing natural world. Living where development gradually encroaches on native habitat and human activity and wilderness intersect, I witness moments of fragile balance and quiet tension prompting reflection on continuity, loss and change. While grounded in lived observation, my work is also informed by an awareness of broader environmental shifts unfolding globally. Counter to this, the comforting rhythm of spring, summer, autumn, and winter provides a measure through which time can be seen and felt. Lydia Viscardi Time Takes Time combines painting, collage, drawing, and assemblage, using printed matter, vintage hand-embellished textiles, fabric, and found objects. These materials form the supports and components of my two-dimensional work and wall-based sculpture. Colorful imagery, layered compositions and contradictory elements reveal a subtle humor and subversive undercurrent, giving the work an enigmatic yet playful tone. About the Artist Lydia Viscardi is a mixed media artist working in painting, drawing, collage, and assemblage sculpture. She was the 2024 Artist-in-Residence at Lenox Hill Neighborhood House (a social services center and cultural institution) in New York City and a recipient of the 2023 Connecticut Office of the Arts Artist Fellowship. artworks.title: The Land You Stand On: Contemporary Art of Native and Indigenous Identity
artworks.description: October 10, 2026 – January 24, 2027 With powerful and visionary works of art, The Land You Stand On celebrates cultural beauty and explores the deep connections between land, place, and identity in the work of contemporary Native and Indigenous artists. Centering Indigenous expression and perspectives, the exhibition extends beyond geographic and cultural borders to challenge older frameworks and colonial boundaries. Through art and programming, the exhibition encourages meaningful engagement with the history and ongoing presence of Indigenous and Native communities. Featuring the work of Julia Buffalohead Aymar Ccopacatty Joshua Carter Renee Castro Hartman Deetz Felicia Gabaldon Guido Garaycochea Julia Marden Marianne Nicolson Indira Urrutia Brook Waldron Co-curated by Brooke Waldron, Cedar Nation, Kristine Holohan, Pattagansett Art Center, and the Lyman Allyn Art Museum. About Pattagansett Art Center Pattagansett Art Center is an artist-run, creative community-centered organization rooted in the practice of wellness and environmentally sustainable models created through the Arts. About Cedar Nation Cedar Nation is a meeting ground uniting collaboration through aligned purpose and shared vision. We are a distinctive group of Artists, Organizers and Knowledge Keepers working together to transform the deficient representation of contemporary Native people in galleries and institutions.

artworks.title: Isaac Sheffield: Portraits from New London’s Whaling Era
artworks.description: September 12, 2026 – January 3, 2027 This exhibition, the first to focus on the work of artist Isaac Sheffield, examines his portraits and portrait miniatures of the 1830s and 1840s, a time of growth, innovation, and change at the height of New London’s whaling era. Born in Guilford, Connecticut at the turn of the 19th century, Isaac Sheffield, Jr. painted portraits and portrait miniatures until his death in 1845, documenting New London whaling captains and their families along with other members of the community. Featuring landscape and maritime views, these portraits hold intriguing clues to his sitters’ professions, education, and accomplishments, as well as their values and familial connections. Portraits from New London’s Whaling Era brings together paintings from various regional public and private collections, illuminating this long-overlooked artist’s contributions to regional art and history and to American portraiture more broadly. Image: Isaac Sheffield, Portrait of Capt. Benjamin R. Latham , oil on canvas, ca. 1840. Museum purchase, 1964.246.
